key_insight: A NURBS level-set framework enables robust, CAD-compatible topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff–Love shells using volume-based shape derivatives.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports lightweight shell design under uncertain loads and material properties while preserving compatibility with CAD/CAM workflows.
method: Model single- and multi-patch shells with isogeometric analysis, including non-matching meshes.
Use the speed method and a biharmonic equation to obtain descent directions without local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming.
Represent uncertainty through Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian random fields.
evidence_signal: Numerical examples reproduce literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined IGA approaches, although the abstract provides no quantitative speedup.
watch_item: Monte Carlo sampling may increase optimization cost; fewer elements alone do not establish lower total runtime.
paper_title: Robust topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love shells by the Speed Method
